newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank - Q1 profit confirms forecast.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank - Q1 profit confirms forecast.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG's outgoing chief executive Hilmar Kopper said on Tuesday that Deutsche's earnings in the first quarter of 1997 confirmed the bank's expectations that full year earnings will be above 1996 levels.
In the first quarter of 1997, operating profit after risk provisions rose by 21 percent to 1.4 billion marks and pre-tax profit rose by 28 percent to 1.3 billion marks.

"We have the result for the first quarter of 1997. It confirms our estimate that the current business year is proceeding well and that we will again be able to present an improved overall result," Kopper said.
Kopper added that it would be wrong just to multiply first quarter results by four.
"The year is still long and there are considerable uncertainties," he said. "You can't simply calculate future interest rates and prices."
Kopper said Deutsche Bank plans to achieve a return on equity of 25 percent before tax and a cost/income ratio of clearly below 70 percent in this decade.
In 1996, the bank had a return on equity of 17.1 percent before tax and a cost/income reatio of 71.7 percent.
